div.l: To Caunt̉erbury warde y mene it so
And homward he shaƚƚ tellen other two
Of auentures that whilom hath by fallen̄
And whiche of yow þat bereth hym best of alle
That is to seyne that telleth in this caas
Talys of best sentence and moost solas
Shaƚƚ haue a soper at our͗e alther͗e coste
Here in this place sittyng by this poste
Whan we comen̄ a yen̄ fro Caunterbury
And for to make yow the more mery
I wole my self godely with yow ryde
Ryght at myne owen cost and be your͗ gyde
And who so wole my Iugement with seye
Shaƚƚ paye aƚƚ that we spende by the weye
And if ye vouchesaf it be so
Telle me a none without wordes moo
Ande I wole erly shape me therfore
This thyng was gᵃarunted and our othes y swore
With full glad herte and prayed hym also
That he wolde vouchesaaf for to do so
And that he wolde ben oure gou͗enoure
And of our͗ talys Iuge and reportoure
And set a soper at a certeyn̄ pryse
And we wole rewled ben̄ at his deuyse
In high and lowe and thus by one assent
We been̄ accorded to that Iugement
And there vpon̄ the wyne was fet a none
We dronken̄ and to reste wente eủerycheone
With outen̄ any lenger taryiengge
A morwe whan the day gan to spryngge
Vp roos our͗ hooste and was our͗ althers cok
And gadered vs to gedre in a Flok
And forth we ryden a litel more than a paas
Vn to the watteryng of seynt Thomas
And there our͗ hoost gan hise hors arreste
And seid lordes he keueth if yow lyste
Ye wote your͗ forward and I it you recorde .
Yf euen song and morwen̄ song accorde
Lete se nowe who shaƚƚ telle the first tale
As euer mote I drynk wyne or ale
Who so be rebell to my Iugement
Shal paye for all that by the weye is spent
Now draweth er that we ferther wynne
Whiche þat hath the shortest shall begynne
Sir qᵈuod knyght qᵈuod he my Mayster and my lorde
Now draweth cut for that is myne accorde
Come ner͗ qᵈuod he my lady Prioresse
And ye ser Clerk lete be your shamefastnesse
Ne studye nat ley vnto hande eủery manne
A none to drawe eủery wyght byganne
And shortely for to tellen as it was
Were it by auentur͗ or sorte or caas
The sooth is this þe cut fel to the knyght
Of whiche full glad and blithe was eủery wyght
And tellen̄ he must his tale as it was reson
By forward and eke by composicoun̄
As ye haue herde what nedeth woordes moo
And whan this gode man saw þat it was so
As he that wyse was and obediente
To kepen hise forward by his fre assente
He seid sithen I shall bygynne the game
What welcome be the cut of goddꝭes name
Now lete vs ryde and herkeneth what I seye
And with that woorde we ryden forth our͗ weye
And bygan with right a mery chere
His tale a none as ye may here

l.hi:
Iam qꝫue domos prīatrias scita pꝰost asꝑpera gēntis
Prelia laurigero
Here endith the prolog of this booke

div.l: Here bigynneth the knyghtis taale
Whilom was as olde storyes tellen vs
There was a Duke that hight Theseus
Of Athenes he was lord and goủernour͗e
And in hise tyme suche a Conquerour͗e
That gretter was none vnder the sonne
Full many a riche contre hadde he wonne
What with hise wisdom and his Chiualrye
He conquered all the reigne of Phemynye
That whilom was y cleped Sithia
And wedded the quene ypolita
And brought hir home with hym into his contre
With moche glorye and greet solennyte
And eek you you hir yong suster Emelye
And thus with victorie and melodye
Lete I this noble Duke to Athenes ryde
And all his ooste in armes hym by syde
And certis if it ne were to long to here
I wold haue told fully the manere
